A_general.open_code_note: The public repository contains the local stdio MCP server and a stdio proxy client for MongoDB's Remote MCP server. It does not establish that this repository is the implementation deployed at mcp.mongodb.com/mcp. Local-code facts below are identified as such and are not treated as hosted-server guarantees.
A_general.release_status: GA for Atlas Managed MCP Server (announced 2026-08-13)
other_official_servers: Local MongoDB MCP Server: separately installed stdio server with local configuration and tool availability differences.
mongodb-atlas-mcp-remote: public stdio proxy client that forwards to MongoDB Remote MCP using OAuth2 client credentials; not the hosted server itself.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MongoDB does not state a separate charge for using the managed MCP endpoint in the reviewed documentation. Atlas resource usage remains subject to Atlas pricing.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Atlas Free: $0/hour. Flex: $0.011/hour, up to $30/month on the pricing page reviewed. Dedicated: listed from $0.08/hour, starting at $56.94/month; actual charges depend on configuration and usage.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP request limits are 2,000 requests per minute per IP and 500 per minute per user. Programmatic access service accounts allow up to 100 active access tokens each; tokens are valid for one hour. Running Atlas Stream Processing processors incur charges.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: User-delegated access is disabled by default at the organization level, except for organizations Atlas creates when a new user signs up. Programmatic configurations can have assigned roles, optional IP access lists, and a read-only setting that is preselected at creation. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without authorization.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: MongoDB controls endpoint and service limits; organization owners configure user-delegated access; organization or project owners provision programmatic access and its roles/settings; Atlas roles constrain operations.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official tool reference marks managed availability for Atlas and database tools and lists Assistant tools separately. `actions.json` records 43 official names: 41 marked available for Atlas Managed and two Assistant tools listed without a managed/local availability column.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The tool reference documents tool purposes but not the hosted tools/list schemas or complete result envelopes. The unauthenticated endpoint returned HTTP 401 with JSON error, reason, and detail fields.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth-protected resource. POST to the endpoint returned HTTP 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="mcp", resource_metadata="https://mcp.mongodb.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`. Resource metadata: `resource=https://mcp.mongodb.com`; `authorization_servers=[https://authorize.mongodb.com]`; `scopes_supported=[]`. Endpoint-path metadata returned HTTP 401 with the same challenge.
C_capabilities.authorization_server: https://authorize.mongodb.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server reports issuer https://authorize.mongodb.com; authorization endpoint https://cloud.mongodb.com/oauth/authorize; token endpoint https://authorize.mongodb.com/tokens; JWKS https://authorize.mongodb.com/jwks; revocation endpoint https://authorize.mongodb.com/tokens/revoke; code response; authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants; PKCE S256; client auth methods none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt; `client_id_metadata_document_supported=true`. No `registration_endpoint` is listed. The OIDC configuration URL returned 404.

The endpoint challenged unauthenticated access with a Bearer resource-metadata URL. The metadata names MongoDB's authorization server. Its OAuth metadata lists authorization-code and client-credentials flows, among others; actual access is further governed by Atlas identities, roles, and configuration.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated request: HTTP 401 JSON `{ "error": 401, "reason": "Unauthorized", "detail": "You are not authorized for this resource." }`. OAuth metadata reports an empty supported-scope list.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc: protected-resource metadata advertises `https://authorize.mongodb.com` and an empty `scopes_supported` array. OAuth server metadata: authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`; PKCE S256; auth methods none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt; no registration endpoint listed; client-ID metadata documents supported. Token lifetimes vary by access model: programmatic access tokens are documented as one hour; delegated token lifetime was not found. Revocation endpoint is https://authorize.mongodb.com/tokens/revoke.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: MongoDB documents confirmation prompts for some risky operations, including aggregation pipelines using `$out` or `$merge`. The prompt depends on the AI client supporting elicitation; without it, the operation runs without prompting. The public local implementation also contains elicitation logic, but is not the deployed endpoint.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: "The MCP Server also triggers a confirmation prompt when an aggregation pipeline contains a $out or $merge stage."
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: If the supported client elicits and the user declines, the server returns an error and does not perform the operation. Without client elicitation support, the pipeline executes without the confirmation prompt.

Managed access is configured through Atlas access models: organization-level enablement and access mode for user-delegated clients, or per-configuration roles, optional IP access list, and read-only setting for programmatic access. Local-server flags such as `readOnly` and `disabledTools` are not attributed to the hosted endpoint.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: "Atlas preselects read-only when you create an MCP configuration."
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Configuration affects available operations and permissions; Atlas documents that write tools are not available to an agent when a programmatic MCP configuration is read-only.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The endpoint's unauthenticated response is a JSON error object; other hosted tool error formats were not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official hosted docs list read, write, and destructive actions. No hosted tool-annotation values were found. The public local code declares readOnlyHint/destructiveHint annotations, but is a different deployment. 2. Hosted docs describe elicitation confirmation for `$out`/`$merge`; it depends on client support and is not guaranteed. Atlas roles and read-only settings enforce permissions. 3. OAuth metadata reports empty scopes_supported; access models instead rely on Atlas user roles or assigned Service Account roles. User-delegated access uses individual identity; programmatic tokens last one hour, with up to 100 active tokens per service account. Atlas documents revocation and access ending when valid tokens cease working. Organization enablement is disabled by default except the stated new-organization exception. 4. Programmatic configurations support read-only and optional IP allowlists; user-delegated access has organization-level read-only/read-write modes. Local-only configuration includes tool disabling and other flags; no hosted URL toolset filter was found. 5. Hosted security docs say Atlas does not share credentials with the AI client; short-lived credentials are used for the data-plane connection. Local code and docs describe credential redaction/storage, but do not establish deployed endpoint handling. 6. Hosted limits: 2,000 requests/minute/IP and 500/minute/user. Performance Advisor slow-query samples are capped at 50. Stream Processing processors incur charges. 7. Hosted parameter validation/correction behavior was not found. Public local code uses strict Zod input schemas; this is not confirmed for the hosted deployment. 8. Atlas says it does not record individual tool calls universally; operations that produce audit events attribute them to the user or Service Account. Public local code includes telemetry, but that behavior cannot be transferred to hosted. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report tool appears in the listed action names/descriptions. MongoDB privacy policy generally discusses surveys and chatbot input/output, but no MCP-specific telemetry/retention terms were found. 10. Assistant knowledge tools provide guidance; no hosted initialize instructions were published. Local code and separate MongoDB agent skills are not evidence of hosted instructions. 11. Past agent behavior changing future outputs/tools/resources: Unknown. 12. Atlas Managed and Local are distinct deployment variants and have different tool availability; same managed endpoint supports user-delegated and programmatic access models. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution tool appears in the listed hosted tools. `aggregate` can write using `$out`/`$merge`, subject to permissions and client confirmation behavior.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: The official tool reference says to use `atlas-inspect-cluster` to poll after cluster creation until the cluster state reaches IDLE.
The official tool reference says to resolve region names or codes with `atlas-get-regions` before creating or upgrading a cluster.
The official tool reference says vector and lexical search indexes must be dropped and recreated to update them.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: MongoDB publishes distinct Atlas Managed and Local server variants with different tool availability, plus two access models for the managed endpoint. The tool reference marks most Atlas and database tool availability per variant; local Atlas deployment tools are explicitly local-only.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference exists at https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server/tools/. `actions.json` contains 41 tools whose official tables mark Atlas Managed availability, plus the two official Assistant tools listed in a separate table without an Atlas Managed/Local availability column. No catalogue-only tools were added. The official reference does not state a total. Glama and Composio listings were checked as cross-checks; their surfaced tools do not replace the official managed availability table. The exact hosted schemas/parameters are not published in the reviewed tool reference, so parameters are marked NOT PUBLISHED.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: MongoDB documents recommendations to use least-privilege roles, read-only access where appropriate, and clients supporting elicitation. The confirmation prompt for `$out`/`$merge` depends on the AI client supporting elicitation; without support, MongoDB says the pipeline runs without asking for confirmation. The tool reference also recommends polling cluster creation with `atlas-inspect-cluster`.
F_documentation.governance_promises: MongoDB states: "Atlas never shares your credentials with the AI client." For user-delegated access, the AI client cannot exceed the user's Atlas permissions. Programmatic configurations have assigned roles, an optional IP access list, and read-only settings. Atlas says it does not record every individual MCP tool call; audit events are generated for some operations and attribute the event to the user or Service Account. General privacy policy covers product usage and chatbot inputs/outputs, but a specific MCP retention or AI-training promise was not found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: MongoDB describes managed access as OAuth-based, with user-delegated actions attributed to the authorizing user and organization controls for enablement, read-only mode, and revocation. It describes the service as GA and MongoDB-hosted, requiring no MCP infrastructure for users to host.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Atlas role checks, read-only configuration, organization enablement, IP access lists, token expiry, and rate limits are documented as service-side controls. Elicitation confirmation depends on the client and is not guaranteed. Audit attribution applies to audit events rather than every tool call. The general privacy policy does not specify MCP-specific retention, masking, or training behavior.

contradictions: OAuth protected-resource metadata reports `scopes_supported: []`, while hosted documentation describes access restrictions through Atlas roles and read-only modes. These may be separate authorization layers; the metadata does not expose scopes for the product permissions.

The official tool reference marks 41 tools as available for Atlas Managed, but lists the two Assistant tools in a separate table without a managed/local availability indication. They are included in `actions.json` as officially listed names; their hosted availability is not explicitly marked.

The hosted security documentation says `$out`/`$merge` confirmation depends on client elicitation support and that the operation runs without a prompt when support is absent. Therefore the documented confirmation is conditional rather than an unconditional server-enforced approval step.
observations_for_research: The managed server supports two access models: user-delegated access that attributes audit events to the authorizing user, and programmatic access attributed to a Service Account.

Hosted Atlas permission controls can hide write tools in read-only programmatic configurations, while a read-labeled aggregation tool can still express writes through `$out` or `$merge`; authorization and conditional elicitation govern that path.
The endpoint's OAuth metadata exposes an authorization server but advertises no supported scopes, while product access policies are described separately through Atlas roles and configuration.
notes: The evidence folder, tool reference HTML/text, OAuth responses supplied in the prompt, and pinned public repository were checked. The hosted endpoint itself returned 401, so its initialize instructions and live tools/list output could not be inspected. The public MongoDB repository is the local distribution and a remote proxy client, not confirmed as deployed endpoint code. Public tool schemas for the hosted server were not found. npm returned HTTP 403. Pricing and general privacy sources are official; no MCP-specific pricing, retention, or training terms were found. A community-maintained unofficial repository was listed in links.json and excluded from evidence.
